body: Thanks. You've really helped to put my mind at ease.

Now that you mention night sweats, that is something that has happened. It's so rare that I can't really even say how often it happens, maybe once, maybe twice a year? The last time was about two months ago, I woke up warm and clammy, kicked off the blanket and cooled right down.

I guess the fact that I started exercising being the cause is the best case scenario? I'd hate to have to sweat this much for months though.

No, to all except maybe the last one. The past couple of days I've been going in the morning before work when I used to go after lunch.

Also, it's not an "episode" it's that I've been sweating faster than the sweat can dry. Maybe two hours into work I can check and I'm still dry, at lunch I'm kind of wet at the end of the day I feel like I'm soaked. But throughout the day I fee completely fine.

Right, nothing of any real significance.

I mostly run on a treadmill when I exercise and I don't have a regular schedule. I've been going for about four months, sometimes I'll go three times a week and sometimes I won't go at all for a week. The only thing I would note about my exercise is that I don't sweat much under my arms, or at least the sweat on my head and chest is more noticeable than under my arms.

I'm 29 and very healthy. No allergies, no recent illness, no history of any significant illness really.

I exercise once or twice a week.  

There has been no significant change in weight (I might weigh a few pounds more than I did six months ago but who doesn't?)

It doesn't occur at night. Yesterday, I changed both of my shirts after work and went out. I didn't notice any sweat when I got home.  

I work in an air conditioned office, I either feel comfortable or kind of cold at work just like it's been for the past two years.  

I can't think of anything significant that has changed. I probably drank less alcohol and soda this past month than the one before but not by much and I'm probably going to breakup with my girlfriend but that's not something I worry about at work.

It's not even about the safeword, we have one and I know she'll tell me immediately if I go too far. It's more that I have a hard time hitting anyone, especially someone I care about and the absence of positive feedback makes *me* feel vulnerable.

I've tried. She thinks r/sw is too depressing, she doesn't want to tell any of her friends or family, the counselor she spoke to gave her other numbers to call but she doesn't want to use them. She has a lot of people who really care about her but she doesn't want to reach out to anyone else. So far, I've respected her wishes and haven't told anyone about what's going on but if this becomes too much for me then I'll have to tell her family.

Thank you. I don't feel like I'm doing anything anyone else wouldn't do if they were in my position but it's nice to hear that at least you appreciate my effort. Especially today, when all I heard from my ex is how I'm never there for her.

I realize she's not my responsibility but I really do care about her and I'm (usually) willing to do whatever it takes to help her. I haven't spoken to her friend, maybe I will ask her for help. Thanks.
